日本の大手企業を担当するハイタッチのセールスエンジニア（ソリューションエンジニア / プリセールスエンジニア）を募集します。エンドポイントからクラウド、アイデンティティ、Next-Gen SIEM まで、単一プラットフォームで提供する幅広いソリューションの提案と PoV（評価導入）を通じて、担当するエンタープライズ顧客を技術的にリードする役割です。

このポジションの特徴：

- エンタープライズ顧客に深く関与する、ハイタッチ SE のロールです。多数の案件を回すのではなく、担当する大手顧客に対して、技術要件のヒアリングから PoV の設計・実施、アセスメントレポートの提示、導入後の技術的な関係構築まで一貫して担当します。情報システム部門・SOC・CISO と継続的な関係を築き、顧客側から技術面のカウンターパートとして認識される立場です。

- 最先端の製品群を横断して担当できます。エンドポイント（EDR / XDR）、クラウドセキュリティ（CNAPP）、アイデンティティ保護（ITDR）、Next-Gen SIEM、脅威インテリジェンス、エクスポージャー管理、そして AI セキュリティ。これらを単一エージェント・単一コンソールで提供しており、担当 SE はその全体を扱います。プラットフォームの拡張ペースが速く、新しい領域が継続的に加わるため、特定製品のスペシャリストとしてキャリアが固定されることなく、市場価値の高い技術領域を増やし続けられます。扱う対象は個別製品ではなく、顧客のセキュリティアーキテクチャ全体です。

- 市場リーダーとしての製品力があり、誇りを持って提案できます。市場リーダーであるため、比較検討の初期段階から候補に入る案件が多くあります。さらに製品品質が高いことから、PoV（評価導入）まで進んだ案件の勝率も高いのが特徴です。自分が説明する製品の実力に確信を持った状態で顧客に向き合える、技術者として納得感のある環境です。

- プレゼンテーションと技術検証の両方が求められるロールです。まず、顧客の実務担当者から経営層まで、それぞれに向けたプレゼンテーションでソリューションの価値を言語化して伝えます。そのうえで PoV（Proof of Value：評価導入）を顧客環境で実施し、結果を PoV レポートまたはセキュリティアセスメントレポートとして提示するのが標準的な流れです。伝える力と、手を動かす技術力の両方が評価されるポジションです。

- セミナー登壇などを通じて、市場に対する発信も担えます。適性やご希望に応じて、セミナーやイベントでの登壇、技術セッションでの発信などを通じて、CrowdStrike ソリューションの認知と魅力を広げる役割も担っていただけます。担当顧客の中だけで完結せず、市場に向けて技術的な発信ができるポジションです。

- 一人で抱え込まない体制があり、技術的なキャッチアップがしやすい環境です。社内のチャットツールで海外のプロダクトマネージャーに技術仕様を直接確認できるほか、製品領域によっては日本の製品専門 SE（Specialist SE）と一緒に提案に入ります。チーム内でも互いにフォローし合う文化があり、担当領域が広くても、走りながら技術を習得していける環境です。

- SE チームの離職率が非常に低い組織です。日本の SE メンバーは高いモチベーションを維持したまま長く在籍しており、離職はほとんど発生していません。今回の募集も退職ではなく、前任者の昇進に伴う後任募集です。

- 昇進の実績があるポジションです。CrowdStrike の SE 職には、Principal SE（SE の最上位職）、Specialist SE（領域特化）、SE Manager（マネジメント）への複線的なキャリアパスがあり、これらへの昇進・キャリアチェンジの実績があるチームです。

職務内容：

- 担当するエンタープライズ顧客に対し、ハイタッチで技術面のリードとして、提案およびアーキテクチャ設計の支援を担当します（情報システム部門、SOC、CISO クラスが対話相手となります）。

- PoV（Proof of Value：評価導入）の要件定義・設計・実施と、評価結果に基づく PoV レポートの作成および報告を行います。

- 営業担当とペアで案件を推進し、四半期の売上目標達成に貢献します。

- 競合製品との技術比較および差分を整理し、顧客、パートナーへ展開します。

- 本社プロダクトマネジメント / エンジニアリングへ技術フィードバックを行い、日本市場固有の機能要望をインプットします。

- セミナーやイベントでの登壇、技術セッションでの発信などを通じて、CrowdStrike ソリューションの認知拡大に貢献します（適性・ご希望に応じます）。

- SE チーム内および営業部門に対する技術的な勉強会を企画・開催し、組織全体の技術力向上に貢献します。

必須要件：

- セキュリティ製品または IT インフラ製品におけるプリセールス経験 5 年以上（SOC / CSIRT / インシデントレスポンス等の実務経験を経てプリセールスに転じた方も対象です）。

- PoC / PoV を、要件定義から評価レポートの提出・報告まで主担当として完遂した経験。

- EDR、アイデンティティセキュリティ、クラウドセキュリティ、SIEM、AI セキュリティなど、CrowdStrike のソリューション領域について複数の知見を有し、顧客の既存環境を踏まえたアーキテクチャ提案ができる知識。

- 情報システム部門長または CISO クラスに対する提案あるいは報告の経験。

- 英語の読み書き（技術文書の読解、本社エンジニアとのメールおよびチャットでのコミュニケーション）。

- AI技術を活用して意思決定を強化し、ワークフローおよびプロセスを合理化し、効率を向上させ、ビジネス成果を推進した実績。

歓迎要件：

すべて満たす必要はありません。必須要件を満たしていれば、以下は選考で加点される項目です。

- ビジネスレベルの英会話。

- マルウェア解析、フォレンジック、脅威インテリジェンスの実務経験。

- SOC 運用、SOAR・自動化の設計または導入経験。

- PowerShell / Python / Bash などによるスクリプティング。

- AWS / Azure / GCP、Kubernetes、コンテナ環境の知識。

- CISSP、OSCP、GIAC、CEH などの資格。

- 業務における AI / LLM の活用経験、または AI に関連するソリューションの提案経験。

We are hiring a high-touch Sales Engineer (Solutions Engineer / Pre-Sales Engineer) for our Enterprise accounts in Japan. Through proposals and PoVs spanning the breadth of a single platform — endpoint, cloud, identity, Next-Gen SIEM and more — you will act as the technical lead for the Enterprise accounts you own.

About Role - What Makes This Role Different:

- This is a high-touch SE role where you engage deeply with your Enterprise accounts. Rather than covering many opportunities, you own your accounts end to end — from technical requirements, through designing and running the PoV, to presenting the assessment report and sustaining the relationship. You become the technical counterpart the customer's IT organization, SOC, and CISO turn to.

- You work across a portfolio at the leading edge of the market. Endpoint (EDR / XDR), cloud security (CNAPP), identity protection (ITDR), Next-Gen SIEM, threat intelligence, exposure management, and AI security — all delivered through a single agent and a single console, and all within your scope. The platform expands quickly and new domains keep arriving, so instead of being locked into one product as your career specialty, you keep adding technical domains that carry real market value. What you work on is not an individual product; it is the customer's entire security architecture.

- You can propose a market-leading product with genuine pride. As the market leader, we are on the shortlist from the earliest stage of many evaluations. And because product quality is high, our win rate on deals that reach PoV is high as well. You face customers with real conviction in the technology you are presenting.

- This role calls for strong presentation skills and hands-on validation in equal measure. You typically start by articulating the value of the solution in presentations to customer stakeholders, from hands-on engineers through to executives, and from there run a PoV (Proof of Value) in the customer's own environment and present the outcome as a PoV report or Security Assessment Report. Both your ability to communicate and your technical depth are what count.

- You can build a public technical voice. Depending on your interests and strengths, you can speak at seminars and industry events and deliver technical sessions, broadening awareness of the CrowdStrike platform well beyond the accounts you own.

- You are not left to figure it out alone. Reach product managers overseas directly over internal chat to confirm technical specifications, and in some product areas go into deals alongside Japan-based Specialist SEs. The team backs each other up, so even with a broad platform to cover, you can build the depth as you go.

- Attrition on this team is very low. Our SE team in Japan has stayed together, with members remaining highly motivated over the long term. This opening is not a resignation backfill — the previous holder of the role was promoted.

- This role has a track record of promotion. CrowdStrike SE careers branch into multiple tracks — Principal SE (the most senior SE role), Specialist SE (domain focus), and SE Manager (people management) — and this team has a track record of people moving into them.

What You'll Do:

- Serve as the high-touch technical lead for assigned Enterprise accounts, owning proposals and supporting architecture design. Your counterparts will be IT departments, SOC teams, and CISOs.

- Scope, design, and run PoVs (Proof of Value), then produce and present PoV reports based on the results.

- Partner with your account executive to drive opportunities and contribute to quarterly revenue targets.

- Analyze technical differentiation against competing products and share findings with customers and partners.

- Provide technical feedback to HQ Product Management and Engineering, including Japan-specific feature requirements.

- Contribute to broadening awareness of the CrowdStrike platform by speaking at seminars and events and delivering technical sessions, according to your interests and strengths.

- Plan and run internal technical enablement sessions for the SE team and the sales organization, raising the technical bar across the organization.

What You'll Need:

- 5+ years of pre-sales experience with security or IT infrastructure products. Candidates who moved into pre-sales after hands-on experience in a SOC, CSIRT, or incident response function are equally welcome.

- Demonstrated experience owning PoCs / PoVs end to end — from requirements definition through delivery and presentation of the assessment report.

- Working knowledge across multiple CrowdStrike solution domains — EDR, identity security, cloud security, SIEM, AI security — sufficient to propose architecture grounded in a customer's existing environment.

- Experience presenting or reporting to IT directors and CISO-level stakeholders.

- English reading and writing proficiency (technical documentation, and email and chat with HQ engineers).

- Proven experience utilizing AI technologies to enhance decision-making, streamline workflows and processes, improve efficiency and drive business outcomes.

Bonus Points:

You do not need all of these. If you meet the requirements above, the following will strengthen your application.

- Business-level spoken English.

- Hands-on experience with malware analysis, forensics, or threat intelligence.

- SOC operations, SOAR, or automation design and implementation experience.

- Scripting in PowerShell, Python, or Bash.

- Knowledge of AWS / Azure / GCP, Kubernetes, and container environments.

- Certifications such as CISSP, OSCP, GIAC, or CEH.

- Experience applying AI / LLMs in your work, or experience proposing AI-related solutions.

- Understanding of defence acquisition processes, capability development, and through-life support models

- Assigned accounts are larger and of the most complex nature, where assigned quota is typically higher than lesser-scoped portfolio sales role levels. (Size of quota may be relative to complexity and nature of account set).

- Incumbents routinely sell to and interact with executive-level customer decision makers, up to CxO levels and are typically assigned to Mid-Market accounts segmentation or commensurately complex public sector accounts.

- Expert-level presentation, customer service, financial/business acumen, and negotiation skills at all levels of customer engagement.

- Complete, "big-picture" understanding of the business and technical contexts of key account opportunities.

- Driven, self-starter who exudes leadership on set of accounts and compels others to get on.

- Fully adept at consultative effectiveness and establishing trust with internal and external customers.

postings.description:

We use an AI-first mindset as a force multiplier to proactively and continuously accelerate execution, build expertise, uncover insights, and solve complex problems. We’re always looking to add talented CrowdStrikers to the team who have limitless passion, a relentless focus on innovation and a fanatical commitment to our customers, our community and each other. Ready to join a mission that matters? The future of cybersecurity starts with you.

About the Role:

We believe the Sales Development Representative (SDR) role at CrowdStrike is one of the strongest platforms to build a career in cyber security sales.

If you love talking to people and understanding their perspective, are curious about the cyber industry, and take pride in smashing goals, this is the role for you.

You'll join a team that works together in the office, brings the best out of each other and has fun doing it. Success means making an impact while you're in this role, and building the skills to move into your next one.

What You'll Do:

Start conversations.

- Reach out to organisations that don't use CrowdStrike yet, and understand their business and security objectives. Understand what they are worried about, what they are trying to achieve and educate them on the value of partnering with CrowdStrike.

- Conduct multi-channel outreach via phone, email, and LinkedIn, focusing primarily on outbound prospecting while also following up on inbound leads sourced from campaigns, content, and event engagement.

- Ask relevant questions to determine whether there's a real problem CrowdStrike can solve, then book a meeting between the prospect and an account executive.

Use AI well.

- Research accounts thoroughly before you call, so you can form a perspective on the likely challenges a business is facing.

- Use AI to help you prioritise where your time goes, and to write outreach that's specific to the person you're contacting rather than generic.

- Go back through your own call recordings and transcripts, spot what's working and what isn't, and fix it.

- Try new approaches, track the results, and tell the team what you learned. Good ideas from this team end up in the playbook.

Build real knowledge.

- Learn the threat landscape and the CrowdStrike platform to communicate with enough depth and conviction to educate an industry security professional, but also simply and succinctly to a friend.

- Learn the cybersecurity market; the partners, vendors & problems we jointly solve for customers.

- Learn how to take something complicated and explain it simply, so your conversations stay focused on the customer's problem rather than on product detail.

Own your number.

- You'll have a monthly target for qualified meetings booked, and uncapped commission for hitting and beating it.

- Know your own conversion rates at each stage. Understand how your daily activity turns into weekly and monthly results.

- Keep Salesforce up to date and your notes useful. It's how your account executive walks into a meeting prepared instead of cold.

Work with your team.

- Treat the relationship with your account executives as a partnership. You plan account outreach together and you share the outcome.

- Leverage marketing campaigns, assets and events and collaborate with our channel partners.

- Elevate each other's skills through roleplay, peer-to-peer feedback and best practice sharing.

- Work with the team in person - we work 3 days a week in office.

Grow into your next role.

- You'll receive a comprehensive onboarding and solid grounding in professional selling, including frameworks you'll use for the rest of your career.

- There are proven progression certifications and trainings you'll work through during your time in Sales Development. They're designed to help ensure you are ready for account executive, account management, sales engineering or other roles.

What You'll Need:

- A real interest in learning, both the sales craft and the cyber security industry and a positive attitude towards feedback.

- Curiosity about AI and how to use it in your own work. You don't need to be an expert, but you do need to be willing to try things.

- Technical aptitude, and the ability to pick up new business and technical concepts quickly.

- Drive to hit your number and beat it, on your own and as part of a team.

- Clear communication, written and spoken. Listen, ask questions, and be clear about next steps.

- The ability to handle pushback. An objection usually means there's more to understand, not that the conversation is over.

- A genuine interest in building a career here.

- The ability to learn how to effectively use tools such as Gong, Salesforce, Sales Navigator and AI tools to ensure efficiency in the role.

How We Show Up:

We believe in what we sell. Nobody expects you to know everything on day one, but we do expect you to build real belief in what we're here to do, which is to stop breaches. When a customer raises a concern, we don't pretend it isn't there. We deal with it honestly. If you don't believe in what you're selling, your customer won't either.

We also care about how we treat people. We show respect to everyone regardless of their title, we lead with curiosity, and we know when to be serious and when not to be. The aim is that people come away from talking to you feeling better about themselves and about the company. Your teammates should see you as someone whom they can go to equally in victory and when they need advice or support.

If that's how you want to work, get in touch!

This is a cloud security specialist field sales role with two equally important engines. The first is your own: you will define and execute a business plan for your territories, build pipeline through direct outreach, and lead cloud security sales cycles from first conversation to close. The second is collaborative: you will work alongside CrowdStrike's regional sales teams, helping them identify and win Falcon Cloud Security opportunities in their accounts. - Define and execute a cloud security territory plan for your territories in Northern Europe: identifying high-potential accounts, prioritising based on fit and win potential, and holding yourself accountable to outcomes, not just activity.

- Lead Falcon Cloud Security sales cycles end to end: discovery, qualification, technical evaluation, business case, stakeholder alignment, and close.

- Work closely with CrowdStrike's regional sales teams: educating them on cloud security opportunities, joining strategic account conversations, and making Falcon Cloud Security a natural part of their account strategy. Your goal is to make them more successful, not to work around them.

- Engage credibly at every level: from CISO and security leadership to DevOps and cloud architecture teams. You are technically confident enough to lead these conversations, with or without a solutions engineer in the room.

- Help customers operationalise and consume Falcon Cloud Security products post-sale, contributing to renewal and expansion.

- Stay current on CrowdStrike's cloud security roadmap, cloud platform developments across AWS, Azure, and GCP, and the competitive landscape.

- Provide product and market feedback to CrowdStrike's product management and leadership teams.

- Travel up to 50% to support customer engagement across your territories.

What You'll Need:

- Minimum 5 years of enterprise technology sales experience with cloud security or cloud computing products.

- A demonstrable track record of building your own pipeline: you have opened accounts that were not handed to you and can walk through exactly how you did it.

- Experience working alongside and enabling generalist account teams: you know how to align with them, bring them into a cloud security strategy, and make them more effective without becoming dependent on them for leads.

- Technical depth in cloud security: credible across cloud workload protection, container and Kubernetes security, cloud security posture management, and cloud detection and response. You can lead a technical conversation with confidence, whether or not a solutions engineer is present.

- Commercial credibility at senior level: you have led conversations with CISOs, security leadership, and C-suite stakeholders, and closed complex enterprise deals in the £250K to £2M range.

- Strong Northern European market knowledge: existing relationships in the enterprise security ecosystem across UKI, Benelux, or the Nordics are strongly preferred.

- Proven experience utilizing AI technologies to enhance decision-making, streamline workflows and processes, improve efficiency and drive business outcomes.

About the Role

The Threat Intelligence and Detection Engineering (TIDE) team is seeking a Security Engineer to design and build the automation, tooling, and engineering capabilities that improve CrowdStrike's internal security operations.

As part of CrowdStrike's internal Cyber Security Incident Response Team (CSIRT), TIDE partners closely with Incident Response Operations to ensure responders have the detections, data, tooling, automation, and infrastructure they need to rapidly detect, investigate, and respond to security threats.

In this role, you'll partner with Incident Response Operations to understand operational challenges and engineer scalable solutions that improve the effectiveness of the team. Whether it's automating repetitive workflows, building new detections, reducing false positives, integrating security platforms, or developing new response capabilities, your work will directly improve how CrowdStrike detects and responds to threats within its own environment.

This role is ideal for engineers with hands-on incident response experience who enjoy solving operational problems through software engineering, automation, and modern DevOps practices.

What You'll Do

Improve Incident Response Operations

- Partner with Incident Response Operations to identify operational challenges and engineer scalable solutions.

- Automate repetitive investigative and response workflows to reduce manual effort and accelerate incident handling.

- Design solutions that improve investigative efficiency, enrich security data, and simplify analyst workflows.

- Build capabilities that improve visibility, reduce operational overhead, and enable responders to focus on high-value investigations.

Enhance Detection & Response

- Design, implement, and maintain security detections across a variety of technologies and data sources.

- Improve detection fidelity by reducing false positives and increasing actionable alert quality.

- Develop and maintain detection, enrichment, and response pipelines that support scalable security operations.

- Collaborate with Threat Intelligence to operationalise threat intelligence through detections and automation.

Build Security Engineering Capabilities

- Develop automation, integrations, and internal tooling that improve security operations.

- Build and maintain integrations between security platforms, cloud services, and internal systems.

- Engineer reliable, cloud-native capabilities using CI/CD pipelines, Infrastructure as Code, and modern software engineering practices.

- Contribute to engineering standards, documentation, and continuous improvement initiatives.

Required Experience

- Hands-on experience investigating and responding to cybersecurity incidents in a SOC, CSIRT, or Incident Response team.

- Experience developing software using Python, Go, or another modern programming language.

- Experience building automation, APIs, or systems integrations.

- Experience working with cloud platforms such as AWS, Azure, or Google Cloud.

- Understanding of Linux, networking, authentication, and enterprise security technologies.

- Strong analytical, troubleshooting, and communication skills.

Preferred Qualifications

- Experience building CI/CD pipelines using GitLab CI, GitHub Actions, Jenkins, or similar platforms.

- Experience with Docker, Kubernetes, Terraform, or other Infrastructure as Code technologies.

- Experience with SIEM, EDR, SOAR, identity, or cloud security platforms.

- Experience with security telemetry, log analytics, or detection engineering.

- Familiarity with MITRE ATT&CK, threat hunting methodologies, or threat intelligence.

- Experience applying AI or machine learning to improve security operations and engineering workflows.

Desired Characteristics

Successful candidates combine the mindset of an incident responder with the skills of an engineer. They understand the challenges of modern security operations and are motivated to solve them through thoughtful engineering, automation, and continuous improvement.

They are naturally curious, collaborative, and pragmatic, with a passion for building scalable capabilities that make security teams more effective.

- Experience with Cloud-scale, business-critical Linux and/or other Unix-like variant environments

- Familiarity with infrastructure as code (e.g. Terraform, SaltStack, Ansible)

- Experience with Microsoft Active Directory design and management

- Experience with compliance frameworks (e.g., NIST, ISO 27001, SOC 2, GDPR)

Get Data In (GDI) Integrations Content team at Next Gen-SIEM is responsible for building out of the box integrations for 3rd party products to ingest and parse data into SIEM platform. We are looking for a passionate Security Engineer with expertise in data ingestion and integration for SIEM. This role focuses on designing, developing, and maintaining out of the box data connectors for CrowdStrike Next-Gen SIEM, ensuring seamless ingestion of security data from various third-party products.

The ideal candidate has hands-on experience in cybersecurity, data ingestion pipelines, log collection mechanisms, and security event processing. You should be well-versed in industry-standard data ingestion and integration methods and possess strong knowledge about security products and platform

This role is hybrid, on-site at our NYC Office Location. Candidates should be comfortable visiting the office twice a week once the development center is established.

What You'll Do:

- Evaluate, develop, maintain, and enhance data connectors and parsers to ingest data from third-party security products into CrowdStrike Next-Gen SIEM

- Set up and maintain a lab or test environment for security products to validate data connectors and troubleshoot issues

- Troubleshoot and resolve issues with existing data connectors to ensure reliable log ingestion

- Collaborate with internal teams to define efficient logging, error handling, data normalization and documentation for data connectors

- Research and implement best practices for ingesting security logs from Firewalls, IDS/IPS, Cloud Security products, Endpoint Security, and other security products and platforms

- Write and maintain high-quality technical documentation for integration methods and troubleshooting guides

- Provide on-call support for critical data ingestion issues and production incidents

- Work with customers, customer success and customer support teams to troubleshoot and resolve data ingestion-related issues and ensure effective communication

- Bachelor’s or Master’s degree in Computer Science or related field or equivalent work experience.

- 6+ years of experience in cybersecurity and SIEM integrations

- Experience in developing data connectors or ingestion pipelines for SIEM platforms such as Splunk, Sentinel, Exabeam, QRadar etc.

- Experience in security data normalization schemas, parsing and data enrichment

- Experience in setting up and managing environments for security products such as Firewalls, IDS/IPS, EDR, CASB, Identity Security, Email Security etc.

- Experience with security events and its formats such as Syslog, CEF, LEEF, JSON, XML

- Working knowledge of log processing or shipping tools such as Cribl, Splunk forwarder, Azure monitoring agent, LogScale log collector etc.

- Working knowledge on cloud-native logging services such as AWS CloudWatch, Azure Monitor, or GCP Logging

- Proficiency in at least one programming language, preferably Python or Go

- Strong documentation, communication and customer interaction skills

- Proven experience utilizing AI technologies to enhance decision-making, streamline workflows and processes, improve efficiency and drive business outcomes.

About the Role:

You'll be joining our MacOS Sensor Foundation team supporting CrowdStrike's flagship Falcon endpoint protection platform. This team is responsible for core sensor components in user space (C++, Swift). We build and maintain the MacOS sensor, creating and/or building a platform for products and features that empower customers with prevention, detection, and response capabilities.

Location:

- This role is hybrid, requiring 2-3 days per week on-site at one of the posted locations.

What You’ll Do:

CrowdStrike Falcon Host is a two-component security product. One component is a “sensor”: a driver installed on client machines that observes system activity and recognizes malicious behavior, then provides on-box prevention capability and remote telemetry to the Falcon Host cloud. The sensor processes thousands of events per second to provide deep visibility into operations on the endpoint, and performs rich correlation and computation to identify malicious events and blocks malicious activity.

The cloud component aggregates sensor telemetry for each customer’s network, correlates malicious behavior across multiple machines, and presents our customers’ operations teams with a prioritized summary of the threats detected in their environments.

This is an Engineer 3 - macOS Engineer role in the engineering team that delivers the sensor (lightweight agent) on macOS. Engineers in the team own design and development of core features on the platform. Features will cross-cut most core OS subsystems such as file system, memory, process, and networking. Many features are also built in a way that they will have shared components across Windows and Linux.

Responsibilities:

- Design and develop software for deployment on macOS systems

- Own features from design to delivery

- Collaborate with multi-functional team in various physical locations

- Troubleshoot issues with the product as reported from customers responsively

- Other projects as assigned

What You’ll Need

- Can develop high-quality code in C/C++ and Swift, and can demonstrate that capability, through job experience, schoolwork, or contributions to community projects

- high concurrency requirements needing strong use of multi-threading high reliability requirements

- detailed requirements on low-level operating characteristics (memory usage, efficient performance, correct conformance to external standards)

postings.title: Software Engineer – Sensor, Sensor Performance and Stability (Hybrid)
postings.additional_locations: USA - Sunnyvale, CA
postings.description:
As a global leader in cybersecurity, CrowdStrike protects the people, processes and technologies that drive modern organizations. Since 2011, our mission hasn’t changed — we’re here to stop breaches, and we’ve redefined modern security with the world’s most advanced AI-native platform. We work on large scale distributed systems, processing almost 3 trillion events per day and this traffic is growing daily. Our customers span all industries, and they count on CrowdStrike to keep their businesses running, their communities safe and their lives moving forward. We're proud to work for a mission-driven company leveraging AI to transform the way we work. CrowdStrikers drive their careers through flexibility and autonomy while also being expected to contribute to a culture of responsible AI adoption, experimentation, and innovation. We use an AI-first mindset as a force multiplier to proactively and continuously accelerate execution, build expertise, uncover insights, and solve complex problems. We’re always looking to add talented CrowdStrikers to the team who have limitless passion, a relentless focus on innovation and a fanatical commitment to our customers, our community and each other. Ready to join a mission that matters? The future of cybersecurity starts with you.

About The Role:

CrowdStrike Falcon is a two-component security product. One component is the "Sensor" — a lightweight agent installed on endpoint systems that observes system activity, recognizes malicious behavior, provides on-box prevention capability, and sends telemetry to the Falcon cloud. The cloud component aggregates Sensor telemetry across each customer's network, correlates malicious behavior across machines, and presents security teams with a prioritized summary of the threats detected in their environments.

The Falcon Sensor runs on tens of millions of endpoints worldwide, across Windows, macOS and Linux, in both user mode and kernel mode. Engineering software at that depth and that scale is among the hardest problems in the industry, and CrowdStrike holds the Sensor to an exceptionally high standard of quality, performance and engineering rigor. Sustaining that standard requires a team with true mastery of what software does at runtime, at the lowest levels of the stack.

That team is Sensor Performance and Reliability — CrowdStrike's team of debug engineers. Deep runtime analysis is our craft: postmortem memory dump analysis, disassembly and reverse engineering, and source-level analysis, used to explain with precision and evidence how low-level code behaves on real systems. It is one of the most technically demanding specialties in systems engineering, and very few organizations invest in it as a discipline in its own right. We do, because at our scale the answer to "what exactly happened, and why?" has to be exact rather than approximate.

Our mandate goes further than answering that question well. We're chartered to turn what we learn from deep analysis into durable engineering improvements — strengthening diagnostics, tooling, validation coverage and development practices so that lessons generalize far beyond the investigation that produced them, and so that the next analysis is faster than the last. Our work makes the product stronger, and it raises the engineering capability of every team we work with.

We are hiring an entry-level engineer to join us in that mission. We do not expect you to arrive with deep Windows internals, assembly, or reverse engineering experience. Those are skills we will teach you, and you will learn them from engineers who operate at the top of this field. What we are looking for is a strong programmer with excellent problem-solving instincts and genuine curiosity about how computers actually work underneath the abstractions — someone who is drawn to a hard, ambiguous problem rather than put off by it. If you are the kind of person who cannot leave a mystery alone until you understand it completely, this is an unusually good place to build a career.

Location:

This is a hybrid role based out of one of the posted locations: Redmond, WA or Sunnyvale, CA, with a combination of in-office and remote work.

What You'll Do:

- Analyze the runtime behavior of complex low-level software across user mode and kernel mode on Windows, primarily through postmortem memory dump analysis in WinDbg.

- Work from raw memory, register state and disassembly to a precise, evidence-backed account of what executing code did and why — and hold yourself to a high evidentiary bar in reaching it.

- Correlate your analysis with source code, applying reverse engineering and disassembly techniques where symbols, source or context are incomplete.

- Drive investigations to accurate, well-reasoned conclusions rather than plausible-sounding ones, and communicate confidence and uncertainty honestly.

- Partner with Sensor development teams to translate your findings into concrete, well-designed engineering improvements.

- Generalize from individual investigations: recognize patterns, and champion improvements to tooling, diagnostics, automated validation and engineering practice that raise the reliability bar broadly rather than locally.

- Build and improve the tooling, automation and analysis techniques that make deep runtime analysis faster, more repeatable and more accessible — for our team and for Sensor engineers across the company.

- Write clearly and precisely for engineering, quality and leadership audiences. A first-rate technical analysis is only as valuable as its reader's ability to act on it.

- Collaborate with engineering teams across multiple locations and timezones, including Sensor platform, detection and OS-specialist teams.

What You'll Need:

- BS in Computer Science, Computer Engineering, or equivalent practical experience.

- Solid working knowledge of C and C++, and the ability to read and reason about code you did not write.

- Good foundational knowledge of data structures and algorithms.

- Strong problem-solving and analytical skills, and comfort working with incomplete information — much of this work involves reconstructing runtime behavior from partial evidence.

- Genuine curiosity about systems fundamentals: operating system internals, computer architecture, memory management, concurrency, compilers and assembly. You should want to learn these deeply.

- Persistence and intellectual honesty: the willingness to keep digging until you actually know the answer, and to say clearly when you don't yet.

- Good written and verbal communication skills.

- Ability to take ownership of your work and follow it through to resolution.

- Ability to communicate, collaborate, and work effectively in a globally distributed team.

- Proven experience utilizing AI technologies to enhance decision-making, streamline workflows and processes, improve efficiency and drive business outcomes.

Bonus Points:

- Any exposure to debugging tools and techniques — WinDbg, GDB, LLDB, or similar — including as a hobby, in coursework, or in CTFs.

- Coursework, internships, or personal projects involving operating system internals, kernel or driver development, systems programming, or computer architecture.

- Familiarity with x86-64 or ARM64 assembly and the ability to read disassembly.

- Exposure to reverse engineering, malware analysis, or vulnerability research.

- Experience with Windows internals specifically (processes, threads, virtual memory, synchronization, the Windows kernel and driver model).

- Scripting experience, particularly Python, for automation and analysis tooling.

- Interest in or experience with the security landscape.

Our goals are to scale to 100s of PB of data ingress per day, while maintaining best-in-class ingest, search, and detection SLAs, as well as a best-in-class cost structure.

Some of the critical elements that the team is working on improving is our hardware and fleet utilization across 400k CPU cores. The team is also working with our internal asset storages and enabling other teams in managing the NG SIEM dataplane. Success in this role is measured not only by what you ship, but by workflows permanently transformed, adoption that sticks, and teams that become increasingly self-sufficient.

Locations: Preference for candidates in Seattle, WA or located remotely on the West Coast.

- Build integrations: connecting the AI campaign engine to CrowdStrike's marketing stack — work management platforms (e.g., Workfront), marketing automation systems (e.g., Marketo), collaboration tools (Google Docs, Slack), CMS, and digital asset management systems

- Develop the orchestration layer: that manages multi-agent pipelines, state persistence, error recovery, and parallel execution

- Design and build intuitive web UIs: that make AI-powered workflows accessible to non-technical marketing users — campaign dashboards, workflow builders, approval interfaces, and real-time pipeline status views

- Create production tooling: including HTML/email template generation from agent outputs, design asset pipelines (PPTX, PDF, SVG), and content publishing workflows

- Build analytics infrastructure: performance dashboards, agent quality scoring, A/B test tracking, and feedback loops from distribution metrics back into the agent system

- Design, build, and deploy custom AI agents: and agentic workflows that integrate AI APIs, MCP servers, automation platforms, and enterprise systems into our GTM motion

- Implement auth, permissions, and multi-tenancy: so multiple marketing teams and campaign owners can run pipelines concurrently with appropriate access controls

- Own CI/CD and reliability: automated testing for agent outputs, regression detection, deployment pipelines, monitoring and alerting

- Optimize performance: caching, parallelization, and cost management for LLM API calls across high-volume campaign runs

- Partner closely with Performance Marketing, Digital Intelligence, Engineering, and marketing leadership: to ensure the roadmap is technically sound, operationally meaningful, and connected to business outcomes

What You’ll Need:

- 8+ years of full-stack engineering experience with Python and modern JavaScript or TypeScript

- Bachelor's degree in Computer Science, Software Engineering, or a related technical field — or equivalent practical experience

- Frontend engineering experience: you've built production web applications with React (or equivalent) and understand how to design interfaces that drive adoption with non-technical users

- Production experience with LLM/AI APIs: you've built and shipped systems that call Claude, GPT, or similar models at scale, and you understand token management, rate limiting, error handling, reliability, and cost optimization

- Demonstrated experience with AI agents: you've designed, built, and deployed agentic workflows that transformed real work, not just isolated experiments

- Experience building evaluation frameworks: for AI systems, including prompt evals, output quality scoring, benchmarking, and testing against clear baselines

- Strong systems design skills: you can architect a multi-service platform, design APIs, and make infrastructure decisions that hold up as the system scales

- Integration experience: you've connected systems via REST APIs, webhooks, OAuth, and worked with enterprise tools (project management, CMS, marketing automation platforms)

- A strong builder mindset: you would rather ship a working v1, learn quickly, and iterate than spend a quarter talking about what might be possible. You thrive in ambiguity, make smart architectural calls, and create clarity where none exists yet

- Strong communication skills and a genuine ability to translate technical concepts for non-technical audiences

- Working knowledge of CI/CD, containerization, cloud infrastructure, and observability (AWS preferred)

- Proven experience utilizing AI technologies to enhance decision-making, streamline workflows and processes, improve efficiency and drive business outcomes.

Bonus Points:

- Experience with multi-agent AI systems, LLM orchestration frameworks (LangChain, CrewAI, Claude Code agents), or building AI-powered automation at scale

- Experience working closely with marketing teams or building systems for marketers as end users — familiarity with work management platforms (e.g., Workfront, Asana), marketing automation systems (e.g., Marketo, HubSpot), CMS platforms, or the campaign lifecycle

- Experience building internal platforms, developer tools, or self-service systems where other teams are your customers

- Experience building workflow builders, drag-and-drop interfaces, or low-code/no-code platforms — an eye for UX and tools that non-engineers actually enjoy using

- Familiarity with document and content pipelines — HTML email rendering, PDF or PPTX generation, structured publishing workflows, or turning structured data into polished visual outputs

- Familiarity with vector databases, embeddings, retrieval systems, and RAG architectures

- Background in marketing operations, RevOps, digital product management, personalization, or journey orchestration

- Experience leading technical teams or influencing technical direction across functions

- Contributions to open-source AI or automation projects, or a track record of strong technical writing

- Programming/Scripting: experience coding in Powershell, C, C#, VB, Python, Perl, Ruby on Rails, and.NET.

BA or BS / MA or MS degree in Computer Science, Computer Engineering, Math, Information Security, Information Assurance, Information Security Management, Intelligence Studies, Cybersecurity, Cybersecurity Policy, or a related field.

- At least one relevant security certification

The ideal candidate will have 3-5 years of hands-on threat hunting experience in cloud environments, preferably AWS.

You will work with complex, high-profile organizations across the globe, conducting threat hunting in cloud environments to identify active and historical threats, reviewing cloud control plane configurations, and providing technical recommendations to reduce adversary opportunity in target environments.

What You’ll Do:

- Utilize the Falcon platform and threat intelligence to analyze cloud logs and identify historical and active threats.

- Baseline and review cloud security configurations, looking for anomalies associated with threat activity.

- Develop queries and scripts to work with large volumes of data, including correlating data across multiple sources and identifying outliers that may be indicative of threat activity.

- Produce high-quality written and verbal reports, presentations, recommendations, and findings for key stakeholders, including customer management, regulators, and legal counsel.

Technical Skills:

- An in-depth understanding of cloud adversary Tactics, Techniques, and Procedures (TTPs), including attack path chaining and enriching data with threat intelligence.

- An in-depth understanding of the AWS platform, including the following domains: logging, identity, networking, workload security, data security, and multi-account management practices.

- A solid grasp of AWS security architecture patterns, including log management architecture and automation patterns leveraging AWS-native services.

- A strong knowledge of security configuration and architecture of CI/CD pipelines

- A strong ability to write modular scripts and software tools in Python or Go to work with AWS services and Falcon APIs.

- Proven experience utilizing AI technologies to enhance decision-making, streamline workflows and processes, improve efficiency and drive business outcomes.

Communication Skills:

- A strong ability to verbally communicate technical concepts and findings in plain English to technical and non-technical audiences, including CISO-level stakeholders.

- Excellent technical writing skills and ability to produce high-quality written reports and presentations for internal stakeholders and CrowdStrike clients.

- Attention to details, time management, delegation. This is a consulting role and excellent organizational skills are non-negotiable.

We care about what you know and what you can do, not the specific path you took to get here. Strong candidates will have built real depth in cloud platforms and security over time - whether through years in dedicated security roles, a background in cloud engineering or DevOps that shifted toward threat hunting, or any other route that got them to the same place. Ready to join a mission that matters? The future of cybersecurity starts with you.

About the Role:

This is a full stack backend engineering position on the Spotlight platform team. You will design, build, and operate the cloud-native services and infrastructure that power CrowdStrike's endpoint vulnerability assessment capabilities at global scale. This role requires a strong focus on distributed systems, service reliability, scalability, and cloud architecture across AWS and GCP.

This role also requires reasoning and judgment over large volumes of continuously changing data, at the scale CrowdStrike operates — work that conventional rule-based systems have only partially addressed. We're treating agentic reasoning as a core architectural element rather than a feature layered onto an existing system, which means real decisions are still open: where reasoning belongs, where determinism is the better answer, and how to make either hold up in production.

The Product and Platform:

Falcon Vulnerability Assessment is the industry's first scan-less endpoint vulnerability assessment solution, delivering real-time, zero-impact assessments of endpoint security posture. Falcon Vulnerabiity Assessment adds preparation and readiness to the unparalleled prevention, detection and response provided by the Falcon platform, resulting in a stronger security posture and unprecedented breach protection.

CrowdStrike Falcon is a two-component security product. One component is a "sensor", which is a lightweight agent installed on client machines that observes system activity and recognizes malicious behavior, then provides on-box prevention capability and remote telemetry to the Falcon cloud. The cloud component aggregates sensor telemetry for each customer's network, can correlate malicious behavior across multiple machines, and presents our customers' operations teams with a prioritized summary of the threats detected in their environments.

What You'll Do:

- Design and build high-throughput, low-latency backend services and APIs in Golang and Python

- Architect and operate cloud-native infrastructure across AWS and GCP at scale (S3, SQS, Kubernetes/KEDA, and more)

- Build and maintain Kafka-based event streaming pipelines for near-real-time vulnerability event processing

- Drive backend engineering and process automation across the platform

- Partner with security researchers and platform teams (Intel, EPP) to deliver integrated capabilities

- Own service reliability — performance profiling, incident response, and root cause analysis on time-sensitive production issues

- Continuously re-engineer for improved architecture, performance, and stability

- Write high-quality, well-tested, production-ready code with a focus on observability and operability

- Build agentic capabilities into the product — systems that reason over real data, use tools, and produce explainable results customers can act on

- Take AI capabilities from prototype to production, owning latency, cost, correctness, and evaluation

- Design the guardrails and policies that make autonomous reasoning safe for enterprise customers

What You'll Need:

- 8-12 years of backend engineering experience.

- Solid experience with Golang/Java in production systems.

- Strong understanding of distributed systems, microservices, and event-driven architectures.

- Hands-on experience with AWS cloud services (S3, SQS, and similar)

- Experience with Kafka or other event streaming platforms.

- Strong database skills — Cassandra, Elasticsearch/OpenSearch, Redis, or similar distributed data stores.

- Hands-on use of frontier-model SDKs (Anthropic, OpenAI, or similar) and AI-assisted development tools, with a realistic view of their capabilities and limits.

- Proven experience utilizing AI technologies to enhance decision-making, streamline workflows and processes, improve efficiency and drive business outcomes.

- Ability to communicate effectively at all levels of an organization

- Strong collaboration skills and experience working in a global team

- Commitment to software quality — unit tested, code reviewed, and continuously integrated

Bonus Points:

About the Role:

CrowdStrike Falcon Host is a two-component security product. One component is a “sensor”, which is a driver installed on client machines that observes system activity and recognizes malicious behavior, then provides on-box prevention capability and remote telemetry to the Falcon Host cloud. The cloud component aggregates sensor telemetry for each customer’s network can correlate malicious behavior across multiple machines and presents our customers’ operations teams with a prioritized summary of the threats detected in their environments.

Join CrowdStrike and become a key leader in building the most innovative endpoint security solution in the world. Our sensor development team is responsible for building the endpoint sensor which deploys on multiple platforms including Windows, Mac, and Linux. As a Software Engineer, you will be expected to have ownership over major components and development projects.

You will be required to assist with architecting solutions and support in implementing our core features. Features will cross-cut most core OS subsystems such as file system, memory and process, and networking and will require basic understanding of how AI agents work. Many features are also built in a way that they will have shared components across multiple platforms. You need to be able to lead projects efficiently while maximizing performance and minimizing costs, making sure high standards are being followed when it comes to design, coding quality, and unit and component testing.

PLEASE NOTE: This role is hybrid, requiring 2-3 days per week on-site at one of the posted locations.

What You'll Do:

- Provide partnership in the windows kernel mode sensor development team involved in architecture, strategy, in building and improving next-generation Anti-Virus and Enhanced Detection and Response Security Software.

- Develop new product concepts.

- Support development teams in designing and building software with cross-platform deliverables (Windows, Mac, Linux).

- Own features from design to delivery including participation in product demo at the end of the sprint.

- Collaborate with multi-functional teams in various locations across the globe.

What You'll Need:

- Strong low-level OS internals in either Windows, Mac OS, or Linux.

- In depth knowledge with C++ and Windows OS Kernel Development.

- Experience debugging memory corruptions, process contentions and system performance.

- Experience working with teams to ship major features and releases.

- Lead, mentor, communicate, collaborate, and work effectively in a distributed team.

About the Role:

Our mission is to make all of our customers' security-relevant data continuously available for automated detection and response, threat hunting, and other Falcon platform use cases. To enable this, the systems behind NG-SIEM (next-generation security information and event management) are growing to accommodate >100 PB of event and action data ingested every day, up to 10 years of retention, and dozens of millions of queries per hour across large sections of the data stored, for tens of thousands of customers. As a Senior Engineer II on the newly established NG-SIEM EPICS (End-to-End Performance, Incident-response, Cost, and Scaling) team, you will own the reliability and scalability of the security industry's largest SIEM platform — treating these as software engineering problems rather than purely operational ones.

The NG-SIEM platform comprises many decoupled components interacting across complex pipelines. As we scale, ensuring end-to-end health across ingest, search, and workflow execution requires deep cross-service expertise and coordinated action. You will be the engineer who builds the observability, automation, and scaling systems that keep the entire platform performing — not just individual components. You will join a distributed team of high-ownership technical leaders who share a strong passion for our mission: to stop breaches.

This is a hybrid opportunity, with the expectation to be in our Austin, TX office 2-3x a week.

What You'll Do:

- End-to-end observability: Design, build, and maintain monitoring and synthetic test suites that provide deep visibility into the health of the entire NG-SIEM pipeline — from ingest through search and workflow execution — enabling rapid root cause analysis across component boundaries.

- Coordinated scaling: Engineer orchestrated scaling solutions that treat the NG-SIEM pipeline as a unified system, proportionally increasing resources across all dependent components (Kafka, ingest pipelines, downstream services) to eliminate cascading bottleneck patterns.

- Incident response engineering: Serve as a subject matter expert during platform-wide incidents (P2 and above), applying cross-service knowledge to diagnose and resolve multi-component failures. Partake in follow-the-sun on-call rotations, providing incident commander coordination for critical platform-wide events.

- Capacity planning and cost management: Build and refine models for end-to-end capacity forecasting that account for all pipeline dimensions, including partner team dependencies (data services, GPS). Develop tooling to continuously track and surface cost drivers across the platform.

- Automation and runbooks: Transform manual standard operating procedures into automated remediation workflows — including pipeline-wide scaling responses, CID rebalancing, and infrastructure healing — with the goal of resolving issues before customers are impacted.

- Cross-team collaboration: Partner with cell-level teams, product engineering, GDI/3PI, and external stakeholders (e.g., CSM) to triage SLO breaches, drive problem management for large reliability efforts, and ensure consistent communication during incidents.

- Platform improvements: Use your broad NG-SIEM knowledge to identify and drive systemic improvements across teams, contributing to the platform's long-term resilience and efficiency.

What You'll Need:

- U.S. citizen or Permanent Resident and work solely from U.S. soil

- A passion for reliability engineering and curiosity about how large-scale running systems behave under pressure;

- 10+ years of experience in software engineering, site reliability engineering, or platform engineering, with significant time spent on large-scale distributed systems, and the ability to make pragmatic tradeoffs between short-term delivery needs and long-term platform goals;

- Strong proficiency in at least one systems programming language (Go, Java, Rust, or C++) and one scripting language (Python, Bash);

- Deep experience with end-to-end observability — building monitoring pipelines, defining SLIs/SLOs, and creating dashboards that drive actionable insights across multi-service architectures;

- Demonstrated ability to diagnose and resolve complex incidents spanning multiple distributed components operating 24/7;

- Experience with coordinated capacity planning and scaling for systems with significant infrastructure footprints;

- Hands-on experience with streaming platforms (Kafka or similar) and understanding of back pressure, partition management, and consumer group dynamics at scale;

- Familiarity with infrastructure-as-code, CI/CD pipelines, and automated deployment practices;

- A can-do attitude — you thrive collaborating in a team and are not afraid of taking on responsibilities;

- Strong written and verbal communication skills — you will lead incident communications and produce post-incident analyses that drive lasting improvements;

- Comfort working across time zones with globally distributed teams.

- Proven experience utilizing AI technologies to enhance decision-making, streamline workflows and processes, improve efficiency and drive business outcomes.

Bonus Points:

- Experience in a similar reliability or platform engineering role at a hyperscaler (AWS, Azure, GCP) or large-scale SaaS provider;

- Track record of building automated remediation and self-healing infrastructure;

- Experience with cost modeling and unit economics for large compute and storage footprints;

- Familiarity with cloud-native architectures and serverless computing paradigms;

- Hands-on experience operating platforms processing over 1 trillion events per day or more than 10 PB of data per day;

- Exposure to or experience with Log Management, cybersecurity products, or security operations workflows;

- Experience with disaster recovery planning and execution for multi-region systems.

You will own the most complex performance investigations, shape the team's diagnostic tooling, and serve as an architectural voice for how the Falcon sensor interacts with Windows subsystems at the lowest levels.

CrowdStrike protects the world's most critical enterprises. The Sensor Performance Engineering team ensures the Falcon sensor does that without impacting the performance of the systems it protects. This role sits at the intersection of kernel engineering, performance science and customer impact — where the problems are genuinely hard, the stakes are high, and the work directly shapes the experience of some of the largest deployments in the world.

- Perform WPA/ETL analysis for customer support cases and internal benchmarking, including ETWReader-based bottleneck identification and per-component CPU attribution across sensor subsystems.

- Review and author PRs targeting Windows sensor performance improvements: load image callbacks, registry filter drivers, and process/thread notification routines.

- Identify sensor observability gaps and push for tooling to close them.

- 10+ years of hands-on Windows kernel-mode development or deep Windows systems engineering

- Expert-level proficiency with Windows Performance Analyzer (WPA), xperf, ETW/WPP tracing, and ETL file analysis — including stack attribution, CPU sampling, and per-component time accounting

- Strong working knowledge of Windows kernel APIs relevant to endpoint security: registry filter manager callbacks, process/thread notification callbacks, load image callbacks, access token and impersonation APIs

- Experience navigating complex multi-process interactions: file I/O storms, SCM/RPC-driven registry operations, process enumeration overhead, and their cascading effects on application performance

- Proven experience utilizing AI technologies to enhance decision-making, streamline workflows and processes, improve efficiency and drive business outcomes.

About the Role:

Our mission is to make all of our customers' security-relevant data continuously available for automated detection and response, threat hunting, and other Falcon platform use cases. To enable this, the systems behind NG-SIEM (next-generation security information and event management) are growing to accommodate >100 PB of event and action data ingested every day, up to 10 years of retention, and dozens of millions of queries per hour across large sections of the data stored, for tens of thousands of customers. As a Senior Engineer on the NG-SIEM Serverless Cell Platform team, you will be responsible for ensuring the health, performance, and reliability of cell infrastructure — operating the security industry's largest SIEM platform while building the automation and self-healing systems that enable it to scale seamlessly.

The NG-SIEM platform is built on a cell-based architecture where each cell is a self-contained LogScale cluster serving customer data. As we scale toward hundreds of petabytes per day, you will own the operational management of these cells through monitoring, incident response, capacity planning, and continuous improvement — while also developing automation systems that reduce toil and enable the fleet to self-heal. You will participate in follow-the-sun on-call rotations (8x7), perform version upgrades and scaling operations, optimize resource utilization, and write Go microservices that transform manual operational procedures into robust, automated workflows. You will join a distributed team of high-ownership technical leaders who share a strong passion for our mission: to stop breaches.

This role is based in Australia and is fully remote. Many team members are located in Sydney.

What You'll Do:

- Monitor and maintain the health, performance, and reliability of LogScale cells. Respond to incidents and participate in follow-the-sun on-call rotations with team support and clear escalation paths.

- Upgrade LogScale clusters and microservices using ring-based rollout strategies. Deploy patches, update configurations, and recover cells when failures occur.

- Build and maintain monitoring with defined Service Level Indicators. Implement alerting, synthetic test suites, and operational dashboards for rapid troubleshooting and root cause analysis.

- Write Go microservices and automation scripts that transform manual operational procedures into automated workflows, reducing toil and enabling self-healing capabilities.

- Work closely with product engineering and customer support teams to troubleshoot production issues and coordinate changes across the platform.

- Learn and grow through mentorship opportunities, knowledge-sharing sessions, and exposure to large-scale distributed systems engineering challenges.

What You'll Need:

- A passion for reliability engineering and operational excellence, with strong understanding of how large-scale distributed systems behave under pressure;

- 7+ years of experience in site reliability engineering, platform engineering, or infrastructure operations, with significant time operating and improving distributed systems at scale;

- Experience with capacity planning, resource optimization, and scaling operations for large-scale infrastructure;

- Proficiency in at least one programming language (Go, Python, Java, or similar) for writing automation scripts and microservices;

- Experience with cloud infrastructure (AWS, OCI, or GCP) including compute, storage, networking, and infrastructure-as-code (Terraform, Pulumi, or similar);

- A can-do attitude — you thrive collaborating in a team and are not afraid of taking on responsibilities;

- Strong written and verbal communication skills for writing runbooks, incident reports, and collaborating with teams across time zones;

- Ability to make pragmatic tradeoffs between operational stability and feature delivery needs.

- Proven experience utilizing AI technologies to enhance decision-making, streamline workflows and processes, improve efficiency and drive business outcomes.

If you meet most but not all of these qualifications, we still encourage you to apply.

Bonus Points:

- Hands-on experience building monitoring systems, defining SLIs/SLOs, creating dashboards, and implementing alerting;

- Strong troubleshooting and root cause analysis skills across distributed system components;

- Experience operating database infrastructure, log management platforms, search systems, or SIEM platforms at scale;

- Track record of building automation that enables self-healing infrastructure and reduces operational toil;

The Falcon Secure Access (FSA) team at CrowdStrike is expanding. As a Senior Software Engineer on our team, you will architect and deliver a next-generation secure access platform that converges Zero Trust Network Access with browser-native security.

You'll build the core systems that enable users to seamlessly and securely access internal sites, private applications, and cloud resources directly from the browser — without legacy VPNs or remote desktops — while enforcing real-time protection against zero-day exploits, phishing, data exfiltration, and unauthorized access.

- Build browser-native security components — develop browser extensions and agents (Chrome, Edge, Firefox etc.) that enforce data protection, prevent data leakage, and provide granular visibility and control

- Own features end-to-end — from design through delivery, including deployment and monitoring

- Influence architecture and roadmap — play a key role in architectural decisions, building toward an efficient distributed zero-trust architecture

- Research and develop — drive new initiatives and POCs in zero-trust access domains and browser security

- Collaborate cross-functionally — work with security researchers, product, and platform teams across multiple locations to solve complex problems

- 5+ years of industry experience building high-performance software products, preferably in cybersecurity

- Strong networking fundamentals — deep understanding of communication protocols (TCP/IP, TLS, WebSockets, HTTP/2), proxy architectures, and tunneling mechanisms

- Proven backend expertise — experience designing and developing high-scale microservices in Node.js / TypeScript / Python / GO / C++

- Experience with client-agent development — building complex, efficient client-side agents with reliable server communication

- Cloud platform experience — AWS, GCP, or Azure, with understanding of on-premises and hybrid infrastructure

- Strong research and debugging capabilities — ability to dive deep into protocol-level issues, browser internals, and network traces

- BS or MS in Computer Science or related engineering discipline

- Proactive problem-solver with attention to detail and a team-oriented mindset

Bonus Points:

- Network security background — experience with network-layer security, firewalls, NAC, SD-WAN, or SASE architectures

- ZTNA / Zero Trust experience — familiarity with zero-trust principles, identity-based access, micro-segmentation, or existing ZTNA products

- EDR/endpoint security knowledge — experience integrating with endpoint detection and response platforms

- Browser internals expertise — Chromium internals, browser extension/plugin development, or web platform APIs

Own the finance and analytics leadership for a multi-billion-dollar renewals business — one of the most important drivers of durable growth in CrowdStrike's SaaS business. Joining a fast-paced GTM Finance team, you'll be the subject matter expert for all things renewals: forecasting, reporting, and churn and contraction analysis, building the models and analyses that inform decisions by CrowdStrike's senior management team and support the company-wide planning process. - Apply AI to scale your impact — use AI/LLM tools and predictive techniques to accelerate analysis, mine unstructured inputs (renewal notes, CRM commentary, support and win/loss data) for churn signal, build propensity-to-renew and at-risk scoring, and automate recurring reporting and variance commentary.

- Turn insight into action — size the addressable portion of churn, recommend targeted retention plays with expected ARR recovery, and measure realized impact.

- Business partner — pressure-test pipeline coverage and capacity assumptions with sales leaders; support Deal Desk on complex renewal structures, pricing, uplift, and multi-year/co-term strategy; provide inputs to renewals quota and comp design.

What You'll Need:

- 12+ years in FP&A, GTM/Sales Finance, Strategic Finance, banking, or consulting.

- Proven SaaS/subscription experience with direct, hands-on ownership of a renewals book — forecasting STR, driving renewal rates and uplift, and partnering with a Renewals or field sales organization on a recurring cadence.

- Deep fluency in ARR, STR, GRR/NRR, churn and contraction, expansion, multi-year and co-term dynamics, bookings-to-revenue bridges, and deferred revenue/RPO.

- Exceptional analytical and quantitative skills — able to structure ambiguous problems independently, work with large and imperfect datasets, and reach a defensible conclusion without a template. Advanced Excel/Sheets modeling and SQL required; Python a plus.

- Demonstrated use of AI tools to improve analytical output and productivity (LLM-assisted analysis, code/SQL generation, summarization of unstructured data, reporting automation), with sound judgment on validation, data governance, and where not to rely on AI.

- Track record of forecast accuracy and credibility with senior sales leadership; strong ability to influence without authority and communicate complex analysis as a clear executive recommendation.

- Hands-on with Salesforce/CPQ and one or more of Clari, Anaplan/Pigment, Tableau/Power BI/Looker, Snowflake/Databricks;

- Bachelor's in Finance, Economics, Engineering, or a related quantitative field.

- Proven experience utilizing AI technologies to enhance decision-making, streamline workflows and processes, improve efficiency and drive business outcomes.

You'll be joining the Data Protection Team in our Data Security Product Group, whose
mission is to build a unified data security system which enables customers to identify and investigate insider threats, identify access to and movement of sensitive data, and ensure regulatory compliance by mitigating data loss risk.

About the Role:
CrowdStrike Falcon Host is a two-component security product. One component is a “sensor”: a driver installed on client machines that observes system activity and recognizes malicious behavior, then provides on-box prevention capability and remote telemetry to the Falcon Host cloud. The sensor processes thousands of events per second to provide deep visibility into operations on the endpoint, and performs rich correlation and computation to identify malicious events and blocks malicious activity.
The cloud component aggregates sensor telemetry for each customer’s network, correlates malicious behavior across multiple machines, and presents our customers’ operations teams with a prioritized summary of the threats detected in their environments.

This is a macOS Developer role in the engineering team that delivers data protection-focused functionality in the sensor (lightweight agent) on macOS. Engineers in the team own the design and development of core features on the platform. Data protection-focused functionality centers around file interfaces, including related Endpoint Security System Extension interfaces. The team operates under the Agile development principles and ships frequently.

What You'll Do:

- Design and develop data protection-focused system extensions and associated services for deployment on macOS systems

- Own features from design to delivery

- Collaborate with multi-functional team in various physical locations

- Troubleshoot issues with the product as reported from customers responsively

- Other projects as assigned

postings.description:
As a global leader in cybersecurity, CrowdStrike protects the people, processes and technologies that drive modern organizations. Since 2011, our mission hasn’t changed — we’re here to stop breaches, and we’ve redefined modern security with the world’s most advanced AI-native platform. Our customers span all industries, and they count on CrowdStrike to keep their businesses running, their communities safe and their lives moving forward. CrowdStrikers drive their careers through flexibility and autonomy while also being expected to contribute to a culture of responsible AI adoption, experimentation, and innovation. We’re always looking to add talented CrowdStrikers to the team who have limitless passion, a relentless focus on innovation and a fanatical commitment to our customers, our community and each other. Ready to join a mission that matters? The future of cybersecurity starts with you.

About the Role:

Privileged access delivers the keys to the kingdom and must be protected. Adversaries don't need to break through a firewall when they can hijack an administrative account, extract a hardcoded secret, or ride an active privileged session. Traditional Privileged Access Management (PAM) solutions rely on heavy, friction-filled processes that vault shared credentials and leave gaps in modern, dynamic environments. Enterprises are modernizing their identity management services, moving beyond traditional PAM and vaults, to just-it-time, continuous identity solutions that enforce contextual policies to deliver access only when appropriate, not before or after.

This role owns CrowdStrike Falcon Privileged Access, focusing on eliminating standing privileges and shrinking the attack surface without hindering productivity. You will define the future of how we enforce Just-In-Time (JIT) access, secure secrets, broker isolated administrative sessions, and integrate privileged context directly with our endpoint and cloud telemetry. It's an area with significant scope for a Sr. Product Manager to disrupt legacy approaches and define a frictionless, AI-native PAM strategy.

This is a hybrid position requiring at least 2 days a week in the office at our NYC, Boston, Arlington or Toronto, Canada office locations.

What You'll Do:

- Own the transition to continuous identity and modern PAM: Define the product strategy to deliver market leading, modern privileged access and zero standing privileges across endpoints, infrastructure, and cloud environments.

- Deliver best-in-class user experiences for privilege elevation: Work with Product Designers to deliver multi-channel user experiences that provide end users and administrators experiences that are in the flow of work, easy to use and ideally completely transparent, operating in the background.

- Leverage the power of the CrowdStrike Falcon platform: Every privileged management decision is better when informed by contextual security and business data about the user, their device, and the target resource. You'll work across product teams to deliver privileged access that leverages the rich security data, threat analysis, security controls, process automation and AI capabilities of the Falcon platform

- Be the expert: Serve as the expert for Falcon Privileged Access to all internal and external parties. You will deliver core messaging, enablement materials, demos, and FAQs. You will also engage directly with internal teams, prospects and current customers to gather requirements, answer questions and convey our product vision and roadmap.

- Use AI agents as a core part of how you work: Research, analysis, spec iteration, and customer synthesis should run through agentic tooling as a default, not an occasional experiment.

What You'll Need:

Privileged Access and Identity Depth:

- Hands-on background in Privileged Access Management, secrets management, identity governance, or a closely adjacent technical domain. You know the friction points of legacy vendors (e.g., CyberArk, BeyondTrust, Delinea, HashiCorp) because you’ve worked with their products and their customers.

- Real understanding of how privilege elevation works across endpoint, applications, infrastructure and cloud; and the difference between assigned administrative roles and effective privileged access.

- Direct product experience with delivering just-in-time access through policy-driven provisioning operations that leverage direct connectors, claim-based authorization, and integrations with third party solutions.

- Real understanding of non-human identity (NHI): service accounts, workload identity, machine credentials, AI agents and secrets rotation. You know why securing machine-to-machine privilege is fundamentally different from human PAM.

- Fluency with core administrative protocols (SSH, RDP, Kerberos, LAPS) and where legacy vaulting and brokering architectures create operational bottlenecks or exploitable risk.

- Fluency with core identity providers (Entra ID, Okta, Ping, and similar) and identity protocols (oAuth, OIDC, SAML) and how they can be leveraged to deliver authentication, MFA and claims-based authorization.

Product Management and Communication:

- 5+ years in product management, with proven experience bringing products from 0 to 1 and scaling them once shipped.

- Comfortable driving ambiguous areas from problem definition to delivered product, without waiting for the spec to be handed to you.

- AI agents are a core part of how you work today: research, analysis, spec iteration, customer synthesis, stakeholder prep. You have formed specific opinions about which models, tools, and patterns work for PM work and which don't.

- Strong instinct for simplification: you've taken something genuinely complex (a privileged access workflow, a session brokering architecture, a JIT approval matrix) and made it usable by someone who doesn't live in it every day.

- Able to mock and iterate on ideas rapidly using Claude Code, Lovable, Replit, or similar tools before anything touches design or engineering. When you come to a product discussion, you bring a working prototype or a concrete visual. Bring examples that show you've done this.

- Able to explain a complex privileged risk concept in plain language to whoever is in front of you, whether that's an engineer, an executive, or a customer's audit team.

- Strong written communication across whatever format the work calls for: a spec, a prompt chain, an eval, a one-pager, a working prototype.

- Proven experience utilizing AI technologies to enhance decision-making, streamline workflows and processes, improve efficiency and drive business outcomes.

Bonus Points:

- Prior experience with and broad knowledge of related Identity Management areas (SSO, MFA, IGA, SAML, OAuth, ITDR, ISPM, etc.)

- Prior experience successfully migrating customers off legacy PAM solutions.

- Prior work at a CrowdStrike partner, competitor, or large enterprise security team.

- Experience treating compliance and audit requirements (e.g., SOC2, PCI-DSS privileged access controls) as a product design constraint rather than a legal review step.

- Prior work in adversarial thinking, red-teaming, or threat modeling.
